description: This pattern uses "还" (hái) to indicate that an action or state is continuing. It often translates to "still" in English, showing that something is ongoing or has not changed.
This pattern uses "就是" (jiùshì) to emphasize the verb that follows. It often translates to "exactly" or "precisely" in English, highlighting the action being described.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiùshì xǐhuān zhè běn shū.

examples.english: He precisely does not want to go.
She exactly loves to eat fruits.

grammar_pattern: 大家 / 很多人 + 都⋯⋯
description: This pattern uses "都" (dōu) to emphasize that a large number of people or things are involved in the action. It often translates to "all" or "everyone" in English, indicating inclusivity.

grammar_pattern: 还有 + Time Period + 就要 + Verb Phrase + 了
description: This pattern uses "就要" (jiù yào) to indicate that something is about to happen within a specified time period. It often translates to "about to" or "going to" in English, showing immediacy.

examples.sentence: 还有十分钟就要上课了。
examples.pinyin: Hái yǒu shí fēnzhōng jiù yào shàngkèle.
examples.english: Class is about to start in ten minutes.

examples.pinyin: Hái yǒu yītiān jiù yào kǎoshìle.
examples.english: The exam is about to happen in one day.

examples.sentence: 还有五分钟就要吃饭了。
examples.pinyin: Hái yǒu wǔ fēnzhōng jiù yào chīfànle.
examples.english: We are about to eat in five minutes.

description: This pattern uses "再" (zài) to indicate that an action will be repeated in the future. It often translates to "again" in English, showing that something will happen once more.

examples.english: We will see each other again next time.

description: This pattern uses "都" (dōu) to indicate that something has already happened by a certain time. It often translates to "already" in English, showing that the action is completed.

examples.english: It's already twelve o'clock, time to sleep.

examples.pinyin: Dōu sān tiānle, tā hái méi huílái.
examples.english: It's already been three days, and he hasn't come back yet.

description: This pattern uses "已经" (yǐjīng) to indicate that something has already happened. It often translates to "already" in English, showing that the action is completed.

This pattern uses "还" (hái) to indicate that something is in addition to what has already been mentioned. It often translates to "also" or "in addition" in English, showing that there is more to the situation.

examples.english: He also wants a glass of water.

examples.pinyin: Tā hái yǒu yī běn shū.

grammar_pattern: Subj. + Time + 就 + Verb + 了
description: This pattern uses "就" (jiù) to indicate that something happened earlier than expected. It often translates to "already" or "as early as" in English, showing that the action occurred sooner than anticipated.

examples.english: He came as early as seven o'clock.
I got up as early as five o'clock.
She ate as early as six o'clock.

description: This pattern uses "就" (jiù) to indicate that something happens immediately after another action. It often translates to "then" in English, showing a sequence of events.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ chī wán fàn jiù qù xuéxí.
examples.english: After you finish eating, then go study.
He goes home and then sleeps.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuò wán zuòyè jiù chūqù wán.
examples.english: After I finish my homework, then I go out to play.

description: This pattern uses "别" (bié) to give a negative command or to tell someone not to do something. It often translates to "don't" in English, showing prohibition or advice against an action.
This pattern uses "多" (duō) to ask about the degree or extent of an adjective. It is commonly used to inquire about measurements, such as height, length, or age.
This pattern uses "有点(儿)" (yǒudiǎn(r)) to express that something is a little too much of a certain quality, often implying a slight negative connotation.

examples.english: Today is a little too cold.
He is a little too unhappy.
This dish is a little too salty.

grammar_pattern: Place 1 + 离 + Place 2 + Adv. + 近 / 远
description: This pattern uses "离" (lí) to express the distance between two places, often followed by "近" (jìn) for near or "远" (yuǎn) for far.

examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào lí wǒ jiā hěn jìn.
examples.english: The school is very close to my home.
The supermarket is very far from here.
The park is not far from the bus station.

description: This pattern uses "更" (gèng) to indicate that something is even more of a certain quality compared to something else. It is often used in comparative contexts.

examples.english: This book is even more interesting.

description: This pattern uses "真" (zhēn) to emphasize the adjective, often translating to "really" or "truly" in English. It adds intensity to the statement.
This pattern uses "还" (hái) to moderate a positive adjective, often implying that something is acceptable or satisfactory but not exceptional. It can translate to "fairly" or "quite" in English.

examples.english: The weather here is quite good.

description: This pattern uses "的" (de) to connect a descriptive phrase to a noun, creating a modifier-noun relationship. It is commonly used to specify or describe the noun in more detail.

examples.english: The movie that we watched yesterday.

description: This pattern uses "最" (zuì) to express the superlative form of an adjective, meaning "the most" or "-est" in English. It is used to indicate the highest degree of a quality.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ zuì hǎo de péngyǒu.
Jīntiān shì zuì rè de yītiān.

description: The filler word "那个" (nèige) is often used in spoken Chinese to pause or hesitate, similar to saying "um" or "uh" in English. It can also be used to refer to something indirectly or when the speaker is searching for the right word.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān qù le, nèige, chāoshì.
examples.english: I went to, um, the supermarket yesterday.
He likes to eat, um, apples.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen qù kàn, nèige, diànyǐng ba.
examples.english: Let's go watch, um, a movie.

description: Reduplication of measure words is used to express a sense of "every" or "each" in a casual or informal way. It emphasizes the distribution or repetition of an action or object.

examples.english: He goes to the park every day.
Every one of us is very happy.
Every one of these books is interesting.

description: The phrase "的时候" (de shíhou) is used to indicate a specific time or moment when something happens. It is often translated as "when" in English and is placed after the time or event being described.

examples.sentence: 我吃饭的时候喜欢看电视。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chīfàn de shíhou xǐhuān kàn diànshì.
examples.english: I like to watch TV when I eat.

examples.pinyin: Tā shuìjiào de shíhou hěn ānjìng.
examples.english: He is very quiet when he sleeps.

examples.sentence: 我们回家的时候下雨了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen huí jiā de shíhou xià yǔ le.
examples.english: It started raining when we were going home.

description: The word "多" (duō) is used after a number to indicate that the quantity is more than the stated number, but less than the next whole number. It is often translated as "more than" or "over" in English.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu èrshí duō běn shū.
examples.english: I have more than twenty books.

examples.pinyin: Tā mǎi le sānshí duō ge píngguǒ.

examples.sentence: 我们班有四十多个学生。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bān yǒu sìshí duō ge xuéshēng.
examples.english: There are over forty students in our class.

description: The word "几" (jǐ) is used to indicate an indefinite small number, often translated as "several" or "a few" in English. It is typically followed by a measure word and a noun.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le jǐ běn shū.
Tā chī le jǐ ge píngguǒ.
Wǒmen bān yǒu jǐ ge xuéshēng.
examples.english: There are several students in our class.

description: The particle "着" (zhe) is used after a verb to indicate that an action or state is ongoing or continuous. It is often translated as "-ing" in English, showing that something is in progress.

examples.english: He is sitting and reading a book.

description: The particle "吧" (ba) is often used at the end of a sentence to indicate concession, suggestion, or to soften a statement. It can be translated as "let's," "probably," or "I guess" in English.
The particle "了" (le) is used at the end of a sentence to indicate that an action has already been completed. It is often translated as "already" in English, emphasizing that something has happened.

examples.english: We have already watched the movie.

description: The particle "过" (guo) is used after a verb to indicate that an action has been experienced in the past. It is often translated as "have (ever) done" in English, emphasizing past experiences.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen kàn guo zhè bù diànyǐng.

description: The particle "呢" (ne) is used at the end of a sentence to indicate a question, often implying curiosity or seeking confirmation. It can also be used to soften a question or to express a rhetorical tone.

examples.english: When are we going to eat?

description: The combination of "过" (guo) and "了" (le) is used to emphasize that an action has been completed in the past and has relevance to the present. It is often translated as "have already done" in English.

examples.english: I have already been to Beijing.

examples.pinyin: Tā chī guo Zhōngguó cài le.
examples.english: He has already eaten Chinese food.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen kàn guo zhè bù diànyǐng le.
examples.english: We have already watched this movie.

description: This pattern is used to compare two nouns, indicating that one has more or less of a certain quality than the other. The adjective describes the quality being compared.

examples.sentence: 这本书比那本书有意思。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū bǐ nà běn shū yǒu yìsi.
examples.english: This book is more interesting than that book.

description: This pattern uses "给" (gěi) to indicate that an action is performed for the benefit of someone. It conveys the meaning of "for" or "to" when giving or doing something for another person.

examples.sentence: 我给妈妈买了一个苹果。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi māma mǎi le yī ge píngguǒ.
examples.english: I bought an apple for my mom.

examples.pinyin: Tā gěi wǒ xiě le yī fēng xìn.
examples.english: He wrote a letter for me.

examples.pinyin: Tā gěi péngyou zuò le yī dùn fàn.
examples.english: She cooked a meal for her friend.

description: This pattern is used to indicate a range or span, whether it be time, location, or other contexts. It translates to "from… to…" in English.

examples.pinyin: Cóng wǒ jiā dào xuéxiào hěn jìn.
examples.english: From my house to school is very close.

examples.sentence: 从星期一到星期五我都很忙。
examples.pinyin: Cóng xīngqīyī dào xīngqīwǔ wǒ dōu hěn máng.
examples.english: From Monday to Friday, I am very busy.

examples.pinyin: Cóng Běijīng dào Shànghǎi yǒu duō yuǎn?
examples.english: How far is it from Beijing to Shanghai?

description: This pattern uses "往" (wǎng) to indicate movement or direction toward a specific place or goal. It is often followed by a direction word like "north" or "left."
This pattern uses "对" (duì) to indicate the target or recipient of an action, often implying a sense of direction or focus toward someone.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì tā shuō le xièxie.
examples.english: I said thank you to him.
The teacher cares a lot about the students.

examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhège wèntí yǒu xìngqù.
examples.english: He is interested in this question.

description: This pattern is used to state someone's surname. The verb "姓" (xìng) means "to be surnamed" and is followed by the surname.

grammar_point_name: Auxiliary verb "yao" and its multiple meanings
description: The auxiliary verb "要" (yào) can express necessity, desire, or future intention, depending on the context. It can be followed by a noun or a verb.

examples.english: I want a glass of water.

description: This pattern uses "要" (yào) to indicate that someone is going to do something in the near future. The optional "了" (le) adds a sense of immediacy.
This pattern uses "可以" (kěyǐ) to express permission or the possibility of doing something. It translates to "can" or "may" in English.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen kěyǐ zài zhèlǐ chī fàn.

description: This pattern uses "要" (yào) to express a desire or intention to do something. It translates to "want to" or "wish to" in English.

examples.english: I want to go to the park.
He wants to watch a movie.
Do you want to drink coffee?

description: This pattern is used to describe two actions performed in sequence by the same subject. It emphasizes the order of actions, often implying a cause-and-effect relationship.

examples.english: He reads a book and then sleeps.
She buys clothes and then goes to school.

description: This pattern uses "一起" (yīqǐ) to indicate that an action is performed collectively or jointly by multiple people. It conveys the idea of doing something together.
This pattern is used to specify the number of times an action is performed. The measure word quantifies the action, often indicating frequency or duration.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ kàn le sān cì diànyǐng.
examples.english: I watched the movie three times.

examples.pinyin: Tā dǎ le liǎng cì diànhuà.
Tā qù le wǔ cì Běijīng.
examples.english: She went to Beijing five times.

description: This pattern is used to give a negative command or to tell someone not to do something. It is a direct way to prohibit an action.
This pattern involves repeating a verb to indicate that the action is brief, casual, or done in a relaxed manner. It often softens the tone of the sentence.

examples.english: I'll take a look at the book.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì shì zhè jiàn yīfu.
examples.english: Try on this piece of clothing.

description: This pattern is used to indicate the location where an action takes place or where something is situated. The verb is often one that implies a state or position.

examples.english: The book is placed on the table.
The cat is sitting on the chair.

description: This pattern uses "到" (dào) to indicate movement towards a specific location. It is often used to express the idea of arriving at or going to a place.
This pattern uses "好" (hǎo) before a verb to indicate that the action is easy to perform. It often implies that the task is simple or convenient.

examples.english: This book is easy to read.
This question is easy to answer.
This piece of clothing is easy to wear.

description: This pattern uses "一下" (yīxià) after a verb to indicate that the action is performed briefly or casually. It often softens the tone of the sentence.

examples.english: I'll take a quick look at the book.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì yīxià zhè jiàn yīfu.
examples.english: Try on this piece of clothing for a moment.
He listens to some music for a bit.

description: This pattern uses "给" (gěi) after a verb to indicate that something is given or transferred to a recipient. It emphasizes the act of giving or providing.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ sòng gěi tā yī běn shū.
Tā jiè gěi wǒ yī zhī bǐ.

examples.english: The teacher handed out homework to us.

description: This pattern uses "给" (gěi) before a verb to indicate that an action is performed for the benefit of someone. It often implies that the action is directed towards a specific target.

examples.sentence: 我给妈妈买了一个苹果。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi māma mǎi le yī ge píngguǒ.
examples.english: I bought an apple for my mom.

examples.pinyin: Tā gěi péngyou xiě le yī fēng xìn.
examples.english: He wrote a letter to his friend.

examples.sentence: 她给弟弟做了一个蛋糕。
examples.pinyin: Tā gěi dìdi zuò le yī ge dàngāo.
examples.english: She made a cake for her younger brother.

grammar_pattern: Subj. + Verb + Indirect Obj. + Direct Obj.
description: This pattern involves verbs that can take two objects: an indirect object (usually a person) and a direct object (usually a thing). It is commonly used with verbs like "给" (give) or "送" (send).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi tā yī běn shū.
Tā sòng wǒ yī jiàn lǐwù.

description: This pattern uses the degree complement "得" (de) to describe the extent or degree of an action. It often follows a verb and is used to indicate how well or to what extent something is done.

grammar_point_name: Potential complement "-bu dong" for not understanding
description: This pattern uses the potential complement "不懂" (bù dǒng) to indicate that someone does not understand or cannot understand something. It is often used after a verb to express the inability to comprehend.

examples.pinyin: Tā kàn bù dǒng zhè běn shū.

description: This pattern uses result complements such as "好" (hǎo), "完" (wán), and "错" (cuò) to indicate the result or outcome of an action. These complements follow a verb to show whether something is done well, finished, or done incorrectly.

This pattern uses the result complements "到" (dào) and "见" (jiàn) to indicate the achievement or result of an action. "到" often means "to reach" or "to achieve," while "见" means "to see" or "to meet."

examples.pinyin: Tā kàn jiàn le yī zhī māo.
Nǐ tīng dào yīnyuè le ma?

description: This pattern uses the result complement "完" (wán) to indicate that an action has been completed. It is often followed by "了" (le) to emphasize the completion of the action.

examples.english: He has finished watching the movie.

examples.pinyin: Nǐmen zuò wán le zuòyè ma?

description: This pattern uses "每" (měi) to express "every" or "each" when referring to a noun. It is often followed by a measure word and sometimes a noun to indicate regularity or frequency.

examples.pinyin: Tā měi zhōu dōu qù gōngyuán.
examples.english: He goes to the park every week.

examples.pinyin: Nǐmen měi nián dōu lǚxíng ma?

description: This pattern uses a number followed by a measure word and a noun to count objects or people. Measure words are essential in Chinese for quantifying nouns.

examples.pinyin: Tā mǎi le liǎng zhī māo.
Nǐmen hē le jǐ bēi shuǐ?
examples.english: How many cups of water did you drink?

grammar_pattern: 这 / 那 + Measure Word (+ Noun)
description: This pattern uses "这" (zhè) or "那" (nà) followed by a measure word and sometimes a noun to indicate "this" or "that" specific object or person.

examples.english: This cup of water is very cold.

description: This pattern uses "第" (dì) followed by a number and sometimes a measure word to indicate ordinal numbers, such as "first," "second," or "third."

examples.pinyin: Tā zhù zài dì èr céng.
examples.english: He lives on the second floor.

examples.pinyin: Nǐmen shì dì sān zǔ ma?

grammar_pattern: Verb + 不 + Verb / Adj. + 不 + Adj.
description: This pattern forms a question by repeating the verb or adjective with "不" (bù) in between. It is used to ask yes/no questions in a straightforward manner.
This pattern uses "怎么" (zěnme) to ask "why" or "how" something happened. It is often used to inquire about the reason or method behind an action.
This pattern uses "不是...吗" (bù shì... ma) to form a rhetorical question that implies the speaker believes something to be true. It is often used to confirm or emphasize a point.

grammar_pattern: ⋯⋯是不是 / 对不对 / 好不好 ?
description: This pattern uses tag questions like "是不是" (shì bù shì), "对不对" (duì bù duì), or "好不好" (hǎo bù hǎo) to seek confirmation or agreement from the listener. It is often used at the end of a statement.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì xuéshēng, shì bù shì?
Tā hěn hǎo, duì bù duì?
examples.english: He is very good, isn't he?

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen qù chīfàn, hǎo bù hǎo?

description: This pattern uses tag questions like "是吗" (shì ma), "对吗" (duì ma), or "好吗" (hǎo ma) to seek confirmation or agreement from the listener. It is often used at the end of a statement.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì nǐ de shū, duì ma?
examples.english: This is your book, isn't it?

description: This structure is used to express cause and effect, where "因为" (yīnwèi) introduces the reason and "所以" (suǒyǐ) introduces the result.

examples.sentence: 因为下雨了，所以我们没去公园。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi xià yǔ le, suǒyǐ wǒmen méi qù gōngyuán.
examples.english: Because it rained, we didn't go to the park.

examples.sentence: 因为他病了，所以他没来上课。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi tā bìng le, suǒyǐ tā méi lái shàngkè.
examples.english: Because he was sick, he didn't come to class.

examples.sentence: 因为我饿了，所以我去吃饭了。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi wǒ è le, suǒyǐ wǒ qù chīfàn le.
examples.english: Because I was hungry, I went to eat.

description: This pattern is used to indicate that something is about to happen soon. The word "快" (kuài) means "soon" and "了" (le) marks the imminent action or state.
This structure is used to express "everything" or "anything" by combining "什么" (shénme) with "都" (dōu) or "也" (yě), emphasizing inclusivity.
This pattern is used to tell someone to stop doing something. "别" (bié) means "don't" and "了" (le) indicates a change of state.

grammar_point_name: The "shi... de" construction for indicating purpose
description: This structure is used to emphasize the purpose, time, or manner of an action. It often provides additional context or explanation.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen shì zuò fēijī qù de.

description: This structure is used to emphasize specific details about an action, such as time, place, or method. It is often used to provide clarity or focus.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì zài Běijīng xué de Hànyǔ.
Wǒmen shì zuò huǒchē qù de.

description: This pattern is used to indicate that every time a certain event occurs, another event always follows. It emphasizes regularity or consistency.

examples.pinyin: Měi cì tā lái, wǒ dōu gāoxìng.
examples.english: Every time he comes, I am happy.

examples.sentence: 每次下雨，我们都不去公园。
examples.pinyin: Měi cì xià yǔ, wǒmen dōu bù qù gōngyuán.
examples.english: Every time it rains, we don't go to the park.

examples.pinyin: Měi cì chīfàn, tā dōu chī hěn duō.
examples.english: Every time he eats, he eats a lot.

grammar_pattern: Noun 1 + 比 + Noun 2 + Adj. + 多了
description: This structure is used to compare two things, emphasizing that one is much more [adjective] than the other. The word "多了" (duō le) intensifies the difference.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǐ tā gāo duō le.
examples.english: I am much taller than him.

examples.sentence: 这本书比那本书有趣多了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū bǐ nà běn shū yǒuqù duō le.
examples.english: This book is much more interesting than that book.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān bǐ zuótiān rè duō le.
examples.english: Today is much hotter than yesterday.

description: This structure is used to express a contrast or concession, similar to "although" in English. "虽然" (suīrán) introduces the initial statement, and "但是" (dànshì) or "可是" (kěshì) introduces the contrasting statement.

examples.sentence: 虽然他很忙，但是他还是来了。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán tā hěn máng, dànshì tā háishì lái le.
examples.english: Although he is busy, he still came.

examples.sentence: 虽然下雨了，可是我们还是去了公园。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán xià yǔ le, kěshì wǒmen háishì qù le gōngyuán.
examples.english: Although it rained, we still went to the park.

examples.sentence: 虽然她很累，但是她还是完成了工作。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán tā hěn lèi, dànshì tā háishì wánchéng le gōngzuò.
examples.english: Although she was tired, she still finished her work.

description: Both "要" (yào) and "想" (xiǎng) can express desire, but "要" is stronger and more decisive, while "想" is softer and more tentative.

examples.english: I want to go to China (strong intention).
I want to go to China (softer desire).
He wants to eat an apple (strong intention).

grammar_pattern: 会 vs. 能 vs. 可以
description: These three words all relate to ability or permission, but they are used in different contexts. "会" (huì) indicates learned ability, "能" (néng) indicates capability, and "可以" (kěyǐ) indicates permission or possibility.

examples.pinyin: Tā néng pǎo de hěn kuài.

examples.english: Can I come in? (asking for permission).

description: Both "二" (èr) and "两" (liǎng) mean "two," but they are used in different contexts. "二" is used for counting, while "两" is used before measure words or nouns.

examples.english: The two of us will go.
